claims.claim: Will a money detox negatively affect my credit score? No, a money detox focuses on reducing spending, not on defaulting on payments. As long as you continue to pay your bills and EMIs on time, your credit score will not be negatively impacted.
claims.note: This is a generally accepted principle of credit scores. Paying bills and EMIs on time is crucial for maintaining a good credit score, irrespective of discretionary spending habits.

claims.claim: Can I still invest during a money detox? Absolutely. A money detox primarily targets discretionary spending. Essential financial commitments like SIPs, insurance premiums, and loan EMIs should continue as usual. The goal is to free up *more* money for investments, not to stop them.
claims.note: This aligns with the core concept of a money detox, which is to reallocate funds from non-essential spending to more beneficial financial activities like investments and savings.
